newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures got a late boost from strength in the German and U.S. bond markets to break through resistance at 128.42 and reach their highest level this year, but traders said the gains remained fragile.

Weak German economic data bolstered hopes for further rate cuts in Germany and France, sending March PIBOR to a new contract high, although traders said with interest rate futures outperforming cash rates there was little room for further gains without an easing in call money.
Overall the short end of the curve outperformed long dated bonds and the two-year spread over Germany narrowed to parity.
A trader at a French brokerage said the strong performance at the short end of the curve was one of the factors underpinning gains further along the curve.
However cash investors remained wary of buying long dated bonds because of the potential risks of a rise in U.S. yields after the key December U.S. jobs release due out on Friday.
The trader said domestic insurers, traditionally investors at the 10-year part of the curve and longer, were putting recent premium income into less risky Treasury bills and BTANs.
Investment at the short end led to a slight inversion of the money market curve with six month rates below one week rates.

"I'm quite surprised by the euphoria which is in fact not based on that much. The market envisions an ideal situation (general rate cuts) but there are however, still a number of question marks," a PIBOR trader said.
"I would be inclined to be cautious...but you can't go against this market, everyone who sells gets their fingers burned and buys back quickly," he said.
The spread between March PIBOR and Euromark contracts narrowed to 11 basis points while the gap between the June contracts came into seven from nine on Wednesday.
Hopes for rate cuts were clearly visible in interest rate futures. At the close March PIBOR implied three month rates at 3.22 percent, lower than 3.28 percent in the cash market.
The catalyst for the early optimism in France was the stronger-than-expected rise in German unemployment and weak German gross domestic product figures for 1996.

The tight fiscal outlook for Germany in 1997 combined with the weak state of the economy made a good case for German rate cuts, despite the positive impact on the economy of a weaker mark against the dollar. This could give France more room for manoeuvre without endangering the franc, economists said.

The rally in the dollar against the mark also pushed the the franc to 3.3397, its lowest level against the U.S. currency for exactly two years. Against the mark, the French unit climbed to 3.3740 from a low of 3.3801 earlier.

The Treasury announced it would be issuing a new five-year benchmark, a 4.75 percent March 12, 2002 BTAN, at its February 20 auction. However it also said it would be selling the existing 4.75 percent April 12 1999 BTAN, rather than creating a new two-year benchmark, at its auction on January 16.
The Treasury also said it sold 775 million Ecu of the new 10-year benchmark with a cover of 2.25.
